fr:mainmatter.html:p: Inquire about how to approach discussion of AI slop extensions to Forester that tend to my personal needs.

For nearly the past year I have stopped using Forester. I initially found it quite compelling, but it was not capable of sufficiently encapsulating a broad set of features that lower my cognitive load enough for it to fully integrate into my thought patterns.

Org Roam, on the other hand, is easy to use and has a richer set of "tooling", for lack of a better word, atop it. For instance, management of org agenda, todo lists, and emacs support. I had used org mode more intensively before my switch to Forester, and I've recently found myself returning to it. Despite the niceties of org mode, I would much rather use Forester. Datalog is quite nice for creating custom queries, transclusion is wonderful, there is a glorious rendered version that can also double as a personal website.

I hope none of these thoughts come across as distaste for Forester. It truly is wonderful, but it is not yet the well-oiled fix that is uniquely tailored to satiate my individual needs. I think its unreasonable to expect anything off the shelf to be a magic fix. Over the past year, I've had many thoughts on what I'd like out of a tool like org or Forester, and I've just let these thoughts sit. I hardly have time to do my job, let alone morph Forester into my own personal digital brain.

I think I would also lack the stamina to coordinate with Jon and Kento in properly contributing. Perhaps this is just laziness from me, but I really don't have it in me to make this sort of customization feel like a job. Of course, I don't want to deliberately write bad code. Primarily, I don't want things like my nix, emacs, or Forester configurations to be beholden to external stakeholders. Further, I feel that enough of Forester is liable to be changed that I have been reluctant to lean into things like custom theming or hacking the compiler in a way that might not be easily accepted as a patch.

In tandem with other vibecoding experiments lately (which I should write about separately; TLDR, they have often been unexpectedly successful), I have decided that I simply won't care about trying to develop these changes to Forester person. Rather, I am simply aiming to specify behaviors. If the tool does what I need it to, I am not going to argue with the machine. Bad is good or something like that.

So my tentative plan is to let Claude extend Forester as I need, and I will deliberately aim to not think of the code directly. Instead, I am treating Forester like a black box tool that let's me manage my thoughts and interactions with my machine in a low-friction way. I'm willing to lets the code be AI slop so long as it continues to aid me toward this end.

I have begun this journey today and I now have Dracula theming, wide layouts, a collapsible table of contents, multicolumn, a TODO system, configured the edit button in dev mode to open emacs instead of VSCode, captured much of the functionality of Org roam, and keybinds that let me use these new Roam-like commands in a low effort manner in Emacs. This was all in a single day of me multitasking and using natural language to instruct Claude to write this. I know there is a lot of AI haters out there, but its ridiculous to blindly be a Luddite.

Sure there are reasons to dislike AI: overvaluation that will surely devastate the economy when it comes crashing down, environmental worries, IP concerns, job insecurity, virtue signalling to all your FOSS homies, and much more. Those all still remain true, but none invalidate the utility of giving myself a tool that will allow me to keep my head on straight. That is, the forest/Forester as I need it, not the coding model. Maybe its just the ADHD speaking, but I find these sorts of aides in lower cognitive burden invaluable. There is not enough self-denial and ideological purism in me to refuse access to such help. In many ways, this is one of the beauties of having tools and machines in the first place.

I should likely message the Forester mailing list about the sorts of features I create here. In such a message, I will be abundantly clear on the AI nature of the code and ask if they think it appropriate to share patches. I expect a polite decline, but I think its at least worth mentioning.
